mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the preceding 60 days reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns in the next 20-day horizon.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% and remains above for 60 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 60-day pre-rate hike period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which elevates consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% while PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 in a month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days after trigger, or R-squared of proxies vs. returns < 0.05 in a rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% suggests robust demand momentum that persists into the next month, pushing S&P 500 forward returns to the positive over a 60-day horizon.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative or flat despite consistent monthly PCE growth above threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month coincides with a decline in inventories (not in the catalog, so omit interaction) and predicts a supply-side shock that depresses equity valuations, producing negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant negative return when INDPRO falls by > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 2%, the discount rate is expected to normalize, reducing the present value of future dividends and yielding negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during the preceding 3-month rate-cutting period.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (not in catalog, so use PAYEMS proxy) and a sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) create wage growth expectations that boost equity risk premia, pushing 60-day forward returns to the positive.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE declines for 3 consecutive months while PAYEMS increases each month
failure_condition: No significant positive return over 60 days when trigger is met (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in retail sales proxy (not available, so use GDPC1 as demand proxy) followed by elevated consumer confidence (not available) would typically drive equity valuations up, but with only GDPC1 available, the mechanism is weak; include for coverage. 20-day positive return expected.
failure_condition: 20-day returns flat or negative despite the spike in GDPC1.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (regime_hint), a sharp rise in FEDFUNDS followed by a sharp drop in S&P 500 20-day returns indicates a direct negative impact of rate hikes on equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 3% and remains elevated for 30 days
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not fall when FEDFUNDS is elevated (p > 0.05).
